items.followUp: Differentiate between a solution and a suspension.

rubric.why: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout.
rubric.description: States that a homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the uniform composition of a homogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, often with distinguishable components or phases.
rubric.description: States that a heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition or distinguishable components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the non-uniform composition or distinguishable components of a heterogeneous mixture.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout, and its components are not visibly distinguishable.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, and its components or phases can be distinguished.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and give an example.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the energy requirement, electron removal, and gaseous atom.

rubric.why: The example shows gaseous sodium losing an electron to form a positive sodium ion.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of ionization, such as gaseous sodium forming a sodium ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example or equation showing ionization.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom to form a positive ion.
